neutral_facts.value: The accused, who were the husband, father-in-law, and mother-in-law of the deceased, lived in a house where the deceased resided after her marriage. The deceased was found dead in the house, her body cut into two pieces and thrown in a park. Blood stains were found in the house, and the mother-in-law was seen disposing of the body by multiple witnesses. The autopsy report indicated that the crime could not have been committed by a single person, and the accused failed to explain how the deceased died. The accused claimed the deceased had gone to her relative's place and was missing, but this was proven false. The prosecution established a complete chain of circumstances linking the accused to the crime.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased was murdered inside the house of the appellants, her body was cut into two pieces and thrown in the park, and that the appellants had common intention with the co-accused in the commission of the brutal murder. The chain of circumstances proved on the record against the appellants is complete, and the defence version has been proved to be false, which is an additional link in the chain of circumstances.

quotes.text: The prosecution story in brief is that on 16.9.2006 at about 19.50 hours (7.50 p.m.) PW 19 Constable Nirmal Kumar Patil received telephonic information at Police Control Room that a middle aged woman came on a scooty, and threw two bundles wrapped in bed sheets in Sewa Ram Zilani Garden, Patel Nagar, Indore, and that some blood stains were visible from the packets.
The chain of circumstances proved on the record against the appellants is complete.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the deceased had gone to her relatives' place and was missing, and that the appellants were in the shop at the time of the incident. They claimed that the deceased was not missing from the house after going to her relative's place.

quotes.text: The defence plea that the deceased had gone to her relatives place and thereafter, she was missing
They have taken a blatant false plea.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that in a case of circumstantial evidence, the chain of circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, conclusive in nature and tendency, excluding every possible hypothesis except the one proved, and forming a complete chain of evidence that leaves no reasonable ground for the conclusion consistent with the innocence of the accused.

quotes.text: In a case of circumstantial evidence charge can be said to have been established, when (i) The circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is drawn should be fully established.
The chain of circumstances proved on the record against the appellants is complete.
